correctness.rationale: The exact two-bond perturbation is positive finite rank. Directly evaluated free resolvent gives B=2q/(1-q) and |C|=q^d(1+q)/(1-q), with 0<C<B. The two Birman--Schwinger eigenvalues strictly decrease with squared frequency; the larger diverges at the band edge, while the smaller tends to 2αβ(2d-1)/(α+β). This proves the mode count and sharp equality case, with no embedded point spectrum by free-tail recurrence. At fixed S, eigenvalues depend monotonically on P=αβ in opposite directions, so the unique balanced split maximizes the lower localized frequency and minimizes the upper. The finite polynomial F_d yields F_d(1)=2d-1 and F_d(e^{-t})=2d-1-d^2t+O(t^2), proving the stated squared-frequency edge coefficient. The standalone checker agrees with finite tridiagonal Sturm eigenvalues and verifies 56 comparisons, but these do not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a localized phonon mode one must provide sufficient stiffness at *both* bonds, not merely enough total stiffness. This theorem gives an exact feasibility threshold, a unique strength allocation that maximizes the weaker defect branch for any allowable distance, and a quantitative quadratic detuning law at birth. The statements settle a natural minimal two-defect design question over all positive parameters and integer separations; the budget constraint and second-mode requirement are physical features rather than arbitrary parameter cuts.
